checks.text: Response, breathing or pulse checked within 30 s
checks.why: Recognise the arrest first: no response, no breathing, no carotid pulse. It takes seconds.
Without CPR SpO2 falls about 0.1 %/s and there is no restart chance at all. Compress first, then bring the AED.
Anyone may use the AED. VF is shockable, and a shock multiplies the CPR success chance for about two minutes.
Stop compressions to analyze (the AED detects motion), shock when advised, then go straight back to CPR.

checks.text: No shock on a patient with a pulse
checks.why: A shock on a beating heart causes asystole and cardiac arrest.

checks.text: No more than 90 s without CPR during the arrest
checks.why: Every pause ends the restart rolls until compressions start again, and CPR success needs a minute or more of continuous compressions.

checks.text: Airway checked within 60 s of the pulse returning
checks.why: CPR often leaves vomit in the airway. Check it and clear it (head turn, suction) before ventilating.

checks.text: Ventilation with the BVM within 90 s of the pulse returning
checks.why: After the heart restarts the casualty is not breathing yet: ventilate until SpO2 recovers, or the heart stops again.
Continuous CPR, an early shock and ventilation after the restart give the best odds.
